note: Household notes written by the family, in their words, for a helper walking in cold. The coordinator retrieves these notes exactly as written. It does not write them, change them, or add advice of its own.

notes: The blue cardigan, from the chair. The green one has the broken button.
Shoes go on sitting on the bed, not standing.
Tea after, one sugar. She will say two. It is one.
Tea first, always. The kettle goes on before anything else, and her cup is the one with the flowers on it.
She likes her sandwich cut corner to corner, crusts on. If there is soup, it goes in a mug, not a bowl, so she can hold it steady.
Sit with her while she eats if you have the minutes. Lunch is when she tells the good stories, and she eats better with company.
Her program ends at eight, and that is her signal to wind down. Anything she says then goes on the timeline in her words, the same as the rest of the day.
The porch light stays on all night. Her water glass goes on the left side of the bed table, where she can reach it without sitting up.
Say goodnight out loud, even if you are leaving by the side door. She answers back, and the house settles once she has heard it.
